hints: Find N first: does the force lift the block or press it down? Then friction opposes the sliding.
worded:
1. The figure is missing; the options show N = mg − F sin θ, so the force pulls upward at θ above the horizontal.

2. The upward component F sin θ reduces the normal force: N = mg − F sin θ.

3. The block slides forward, so kinetic friction μ_K N acts backward.

4. a = (F cos θ − μ_K(mg − F sin θ))/m. (B)

5. (D) adds friction (it would help motion); (C) is the push-down case; (A) has the driving force backward.

$$N = mg - F\sin\theta,\quad\quad ma = F\cos\theta - \mu_{K}\left( mg - F\sin\theta \right).$$

$$a = \frac{F}{m}\cos\theta - \mu_{K}\left( g - \frac{F}{m}\sin\theta \right).$$
